rag.name: Finset.mem_sum
rag.content:
theorem mem_sum {f : α → Multiset β} (s : Finset α) (b : β) :
    (b ∈ ∑ x ∈ s, f x) ↔ ∃ a ∈ s, b ∈ f a := by
  induction s using Finset.cons_induction with
  | empty => simp
  | cons a t hi ih => simp [sum_cons, ih, or_and_right, exists_or]

rag.name: Finset.sum_tsub_distrib
rag.content:
theorem sum_tsub_distrib [AddCommMonoid α] [PartialOrder α] [ExistsAddOfLE α]
    [CovariantClass α α (· + ·) (· ≤ ·)] [ContravariantClass α α (· + ·) (· ≤ ·)] [Sub α]
    [OrderedSub α] (s : Finset ι) {f g : ι → α} (hfg : ∀ x ∈ s, g x ≤ f x) :
    ∑ x ∈ s, (f x - g x) = ∑ x ∈ s, f x - ∑ x ∈ s, g x := sum_map_tsub _ hfg

rag.name: Multiset.toFinset_sum_count_nsmul_eq
rag.content:
@[simp]
theorem toFinset_sum_count_nsmul_eq (s : Multiset α) :
    ∑ a ∈ s.toFinset, s.count a • {a} = s := by
  rw [← Finset.sum_multiset_map_count, Multiset.sum_map_singleton]

informal_statement: For any abelian monoid \( M \) and any function \( f \) from the set \(\{ \text{create}, \text{annihilate} \}\) to \( M \), the sum of \( f(i) \) for all \( i \) in the set \(\{ \text{create}, \text{annihilate} \}\) is equal to \( f(\text{create}) + f(\text{annihilate}) \).
informal_proof: We consider the set \(\{ \text{create}, \text{annihilate} \}\) with two elements and a function \( f \) mapping each element to an abelian monoid \( M \). The sum of \( f \) over this set is computed by adding the images of its elements under \( f \). Since there are exactly two elements, the sum is simply \( f(\text{create}) + f(\text{annihilate}) \). This directly follows from the definition of a sum over a finite set, where the sum of multiple terms is their combination using the monoid operation.

id.name: CreateAnnihilate.sum_eq
id.content:
lemma sum_eq {M : Type} [AddCommMonoid M] (f : CreateAnnihilate → M) :
    ∑ i, f i = f create + f annihilate := by
  change ∑ i ∈ {create, annihilate}, f i = f create + f annihilate
  simp
